refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: io.systemd.MachineInstance is a Varlink interface implemented by systemd1-related components. It can be introspected and called with varlinkctl1.

refsect1.title: Interface Definition
refsect1.para: The following interface definition is exposed:
refsect1.programlisting:
interface io.systemd.MachineInstance
# Memory statistics reported by a guest, sizes in bytes, counters cumulative since guest boot # [Experimental] type MemoryStats( # When the guest last reported statistics, in µs since the UNIX epoch lastUpdateUSec: int, # Total memory as seen by the guest kernel totalBytes: int, # Memory the guest kernel considers free freeBytes: int, # Memory available without swapping, the guest kernel's MemAvailable estimate; null if not reported availableBytes: ?int, # Reclaimable disk caches; null if not reported diskCachesBytes: ?int, # Memory swapped in since guest boot; null if not reported swapInBytes: ?int, # Memory swapped out since guest boot; null if not reported swapOutBytes: ?int, # Major page faults since guest boot; null if not reported majorFaults: ?int, # Minor page faults since guest boot; null if not reported minorFaults: ?int, # Successful hugetlb page allocations since guest boot; null if not reported hugetlbAllocations: ?int, # Failed hugetlb page allocations since guest boot; null if not reported hugetlbFailures: ?int, # OOM kills since guest boot (Linux 6.10 and newer); null if not reported oomKills: ?int, # Allocation stalls since guest boot (Linux 6.10 and newer); null if not reported allocationStalls: ?int, # Memory scanned by kswapd since guest boot (Linux 6.10 and newer); null if not reported asyncScansBytes: ?int, # Memory scanned by allocating tasks since guest boot (Linux 6.10 and newer); null if not reported directScansBytes: ?int, # Memory reclaimed by kswapd since guest boot (Linux 6.10 and newer); null if not reported asyncReclaimsBytes: ?int, # Memory reclaimed by allocating tasks since guest boot (Linux 6.10 and newer); null if not reported directReclaimsBytes: ?int )
# Memory state of a machine, all sizes in bytes # [Experimental] type Memory( # Memory size the machine was started with configuredBytes: int, # Memory size last requested via SetMemory(), rounded up to the backend's granularity. Equals configuredBytes if never called or if the backend cannot resize memory targetBytes: int, # Memory size the machine currently sees, as last reported by the backend. null if not yet known actualBytes: ?int, # Statistics the guest reports through its balloon device; null if none were reported yet. Backends may start collecting them only on the first Describe() call stats: ?MemoryStats )
# Forcefully terminate the machine immediately method Terminate() -> ()
# Request a clean shutdown of the machine method PowerOff() -> ()
# Reboot the machine method Reboot() -> ()
# Pause/freeze the machine method Pause() -> ()
# Resume a paused machine method Resume() -> ()
# Query the current status of the machine method Describe() -> ( # True iff vCPUs are executing running: bool, # Backend-specific state string (e.g. 'running', 'paused', 'shutdown'); 'unknown' if unavailable status: string, # Memory state of the machine. null if the backend has no notion of it # [Experimental] memory: ?Memory )
# Subscribe to machine events. Returns a stream of events as they occur. # [Requires 'more' flag] method SubscribeEvents( # If specified, only deliver events whose name matches one of these strings; null means all events filter: ?[]string ) -> ( # Name of the event event: string, # Event-specific payload data: ?object )
# Attach a storage volume (passed via file descriptor) to the running machine method AddStorage( # Index of the attached file descriptor for the storage volume fileDescriptorIndex: int, # Caller-supplied identifier for this binding (any non-empty string; machinectl uses '<provider>:<volume>' from the StorageProvider, but the form is not required) name: string, # Backend-specific configuration config: ?string ) -> ()
# Detach a previously-attached storage volume from the running machine method RemoveStorage( # Identifier of the binding to detach (as supplied to AddStorage) name: string ) -> ()
# Replace the backing of a previously-attached storage volume in place method ReplaceStorage( # Index of the attached file descriptor for the new backing storage fileDescriptorIndex: int, # Identifier of the existing binding whose backing is being replaced (as supplied to AddStorage) name: string ) -> ()
# Resize the machine's memory. Without 'more', replies once the backend accepted the request, and the machine converges asynchronously. With 'more', sends a notification whenever the current size changes, and replies once it reached the target, moved away from it, or stopped moving short of it. Fails with Superseded if another call replaces the target first. Backends without a resizing mechanism return NotSupported # [Supports 'more' flag] # [Experimental] method SetMemory( # Requested memory size in bytes bytes: int ) -> ( # Memory size the machine converges toward: the requested size, rounded up to the backend's granularity targetBytes: int, # Memory size the machine currently sees, as last reported by the backend. null if not yet known actualBytes: ?int )
# The connection to the machine backend is not available error NotConnected()
# The requested operation is not supported error NotSupported()
# The named storage binding does not exist error NoSuchStorage()
# A storage binding with this name already exists error StorageExists()
# The storage binding cannot be detached at runtime (e.g. attached at boot) error StorageImmutable()
# The supplied 'config' value is not valid for this backend error BadConfig()
# The supplied 'config' value is recognized but not supported by this backend error ConfigNotSupported()
# The operation was replaced by a newer request before it completed # [Experimental] error Superseded()

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.para: varlinkctl introspect SERVICE io.systemd.MachineInstance shows the interface definition as served by SERVICE, and varlinkctl call SERVICE io.systemd.MachineInstance.Terminate '{}' invokes its Terminate() method.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: The io.systemd.MachineInstance interface was added in version 261.

AddStorage(), BadConfig, ConfigNotSupported, Describe(), NoSuchStorage, NotConnected, NotSupported, Pause(), PowerOff(), Reboot(), RemoveStorage(), ReplaceStorage(), Resume(), StorageExists, StorageImmutable, SubscribeEvents(), and Terminate() were added in version 261.
Memory, MemoryStats, SetMemory(), and Superseded were added in version 263.
